feasibility_reasoning:
Mostly feasible, but parts of the mechanism are wrong as written.

What works:
- colo. Nitro passes the original CF Request through unchanged (nitro _module-handler.mjs nitroApp.fetch(request); h3 toRequest returns input at h3.mjs:571-582), so request.cf?.colo reaches src/server.ts:239. It must be optional. A cf-ray suffix is a robust fallback.
- nes-layer. replay() rebuilds Server-Timing on every HIT (src/lib/http/documentCache.server.ts:432-467) and L2 entries do not store the header (:470-482), so nothing stale is replayed. Appending new metrics keeps nes-edge first (src/lib/http/ssrTiming.ts:68).

What does not work:
- A Server-Timing 'stream' metric is impossible. The header is fixed before the body streams (documentCache.server.ts:491-505; src/server.ts:262-263), and log emission at server.ts:261 also happens before streaming.
- 'Stream end from the tee collector' exists only for storable MISS (tee at documentCache.server.ts:696, record lookup at :652-655). HIT, BYPASS and degraded MISS have no tee (:599-616, :669-686), so the degraded case from SC-F3 gets no streamMs. Fix: wrap guarded.body in server.ts after line 254 with a TransformStream flush.
- The Workers clock is frozen during CPU work. Every saved sample shows server-init;dur=0/1 and L1 HIT app;dur=0, so module-scope 'module age' is unreliable. Use isoReq plus a lazy first-request timestamp instead.
- degradedBy needs a server-only side channel. src/lib/ssr/resilientLoad.ts:123-152 is client-shared, so it must use the same WeakMap-plus-dynamic-import pattern as ssrTiming.server.ts:21-25, or entry-purity/import-protection breaks. The existing console.warn at resilientLoad.ts:150 already lands in the same invocation.

Gates and other users: no client bytes change, so check:bundle, check:chunks and CLS are unaffected. Editors, i18n and SEO are unaffected. Exact-string tests need updating: ssrTiming.server.test.ts:187-361 and documentCache.server.test.ts:598.
blocking_issues: No 'stream' metric can go in Server-Timing: headers are fixed before the body ends (documentCache.server.ts:491-505, server.ts:262-263). streamMs can only go in the log, and the log must move from server.ts:261 to stream end.

The tee collector exists only for a storable MISS (documentCache.server.ts:652-655,696). HIT, BYPASS and degraded MISS get no streamMs, so the body must be wrapped in server.ts after the guard instead.

The Workers clock does not advance during CPU work (server-init;dur=0 in all 65 samples). Module-scope module age is unreliable, and the in-isolate timers cannot see render CPU, isolate startup or the dispatch hop.
degradedBy needs a server-only request-scoped store loaded dynamically, because resilientLoad.ts is in the client graph (entry-purity/import-protection).
effect_reasoning:
Direct score effect is 0. The change adds roughly 100-200 B of HPACK/QPACK-compressed headers, which is under 1 ms at 1.6 Mb/s, and Lantern ignores it.

The diagnostic claim is mostly refuted:
- For Lighthouse/PSI UAs, isbot leads to allReady (SC-F12), so handler.fetch resolves only after the full render. streamMs - appMs is then just the transfer of an already-buffered body, roughly 0-50 ms rather than 1.8-2.4 s.
- The real gap (2750-3300 ms TTFB minus 942 ms app) is isolate startup (13 MB parse before fetch), render CPU (invisible to the frozen clock, so even 942 ms may undercount), the Lovable dispatch hop, and network. In-isolate Date.now() sees none of these.

What it does yield is per-colo MISS share, cold-isolate correlation via isoReq==1, the L1/L2/render split, and degradedBy frequency. These are real prerequisites for verifying SC-2/3/5/6 (HIT ratio).

Cheaper or stronger alternatives:
- Log the cf-ray request header so external probes (curl time_starttransfer) can be joined to server records.
- Use Workers invocation cpuTimeMs/wallTimeMs if the hosting exposes them.
- Colo is already visible in the cf-ray response header.
corrected_estimate: 0 Lighthouse points directly. It is worth doing as a wave-0 enabler (effort S, low risk) to measure HIT ratio per colo and the cold-isolate share. As specified, it will not explain the 1.8-2.4 s TTFB gap. Required changes: drop the Server-Timing 'stream' metric; measure streamMs from a body wrapper in server.ts, not the tee; derive the cold flag from isoReq plus a lazy first-request timestamp; keep isoReq, uaClass and degradedBy log-only; add cf-ray to the log for client/server joins; take CPU and wall time from platform invocation metadata if available. Verdict file: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-neweustrategies-dc633fb5/8fd9e8e2-d544-5db4-ae5e-c509c5e3ff6c/scratchpad/phase1/verdicts/server-cache--SC-1.md
better_alternative: Keep colo, nes-layer, isoReq and degradedBy, but add the cf-ray request header to buildDocumentLogLine so external TTFB probes can be joined to server records. Measure stream end by wrapping guarded.body in server.ts. For the CPU and cold-start part of the gap, rely on Workers invocation cpuTimeMs/wallTimeMs; in-app timers cannot see it.
